newsitem.title: USA: Cahners Business Confidence Index 66.4 in April.
newsitem.headline: Cahners Business Confidence Index 66.4 in April.

text.p: The Cahners Business Confidence Index (CBCI) fell 1.3 points to 66.4 in April after rising four consecutive months, Cahners Economics said.
The CBCI reached 67.7 in March, its highest level since February 1996.
"American manufacturing executives signaled, for the first time in four months, signs of concern over the nation's economy," a Cahners report said.
Five of the seven CBCI components fell in April. Marketing spending declined farthest, falling 3.6 points to 64.9.
Spending plans for inventory accumulation dipped 2.9 points to 57.2.
Indexes of employment, production/sales and capital spending slipped as well.
The product introductions measure posted the greatest gain, up 1.1 points to 72.1, while research and develoment was up 0.9 points to 66.0.

"Despite the decline in the CBCI, the index is still at a healthy level," said Daryl Delano, a Cahners economist. "However, there appear to be conflicting views on just what impact higher interest rates will have."

Sixty-three percent of CBCI respondants saw the higher rates following the March 25 Federal Reserve credit tightening as "having no appreciable impact." Thirteen percent said higher rates will have a negative effect.
